items.note: Ten-week quasi-experiment in which 118 Chinese EFL learners (ages 13-15) made picture books with GenAI under supportive versus reflective scaffolding (an AI-configuration comparison); creative thinking and originality were measured, but whether they were scored on the picture books or on a separate test is unclear, and assignment is non-random.

Comparative user study in which 45 designers each completed a design task with physical prototyping, standalone generative AI, and a hybrid physical-plus-AI method (apparently within-person); the abstract does not say how creativity was measured or whether condition order was randomized; below 50 participants.

Compares human-human with human-AI collaboration on the Alternative Uses and Product Improvement tasks, scoring idea novelty, fluency, and flexibility (an AI versus human-partner contrast); N and assignment not stated; abstract taken from the PsyArXiv version (10.31234/osf.io/7x2v3_v1), which is the same study.

CHI 2022 system paper: 2x2 study with 64 children aged 6-10 that varied two AI drawing strategies in StoryDrawer and assessed creative ideas and outcomes in visual storytelling (AI-configuration comparison); assignment method not stated.

Compares FIERO, a card game whose interface uses generative AI to synthesize ideas and make visuals, with online collaborative writing alone (N=60), scoring idea fluency, novelty, and story plot coherence; the AI is bundled with physical cards and game play, and assignment is not stated; ACM version lists DOI 10.1145/3831305.

Compares AIGC-generated logo designs with manual design on creativity and efficiency and collects user feedback; it is unclear whether people designed with AIGC (experiment) or AI output was compared with human output (would be context_ai_vs_human); no N; listed as an included study in the Peng 2025 meta-analysis.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page); search notes describe a pretest-posttest design with random assignment to AI NLP writing-tool interventions including creative writing facilitation, outcome writing proficiency; whether the tools are generative AI and whether creativity is scored is unconfirmed.

Preregistered randomized experiment (n=400) comparing no AI help with exposure to one or several AI interpretations while close-reading poems; outcome is interpretive performance and pleasure, not creativity, so it may fail the creative-task criterion at full text; same study as arXiv 2603.06855.

Proposes an LLM agent-network tool for brainstorming AI risks; mostly model-only novelty comparisons, plus a human study in which 11 teams of young chatbot users started ideation from a practitioner-written risk list (control) or the framework list (treatment) and treatment teams identified more risks; number of people and assignment not stated, likely small.

Preregistered lab experiment giving a random half of 124 university students ChatGPT access on novel creative tasks; access worsened creative performance for above-median creative-potential participants, and a later unassisted creativity-potential task was also measured (possible after_ai outcome); may be an earlier version of Zhu and Zou (2026, JEBO).
